problem_solving_method: We chose a simple, straightforward approach using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Python to ensure rapid development and ease of deployment. This stack allowed us to quickly implement all four requirements including vehicle and owner management with 40+ vehicles, service item tracking with multiple due date calculation rules (fixed date, time-based, distance-based), daily call list prioritization by urgency and value, and owner vehicle pages with service recording functionality. The simplicity of the tech stack made it easier to build, test, and debug within the event timeframe.

R1.evidence: /vehicles and /owners - 40+ vehicles with 25+ owners, each vehicle has service items with fixed date (insurance, fitness), time-based (engine oil), and distance-based (brake pads, tyres) rules, including odometer readings and service history

R2.evidence: /vehicles/:id - Next due date calculation for all items using their respective rules, distance-based items estimated using daily vehicle usage patterns, all items marked as overdue/due soon/fine with color indicators

R3.evidence: /call-list - Daily workshop call list showing owners to contact, their vehicles, due/overdue items with reasons, sorted by urgency (most overdue first) and service value (highest cost work prioritized)

R4.evidence: /owner/:id - Owner vehicle page displaying all service items with next due dates and costs, workshop can record completed services which resets the item and adds to service history

team_members.major_contribution: Complete implementation of Problem 9 - Vehicle Service Due Predictor including all four requirements, frontend and backend development, service calculation algorithms, call list prioritization, and service recording system
Problem 12 (Personal Ledger Manager) - complete implementation in separate repository

major_design_decisions: Used React with TypeScript for type-safe frontend development
Implemented shadcn/ui component library for consistent, accessible UI components
Used SQLite database for lightweight, file-based data persistence
Created three distinct service rule types: fixed date, time-based interval, and distance-based interval
Implemented intelligent distance-based due date estimation using daily average vehicle usage calculations
Built prioritization algorithm for call list sorting by overdue days and service value
Used Recharts library for visualizing service schedules and vehicle statistics
Created a simple Express.js backend for API endpoints and database operations
known_limitations: Distance-based due date estimation assumes consistent daily vehicle usage patterns
Call list prioritization uses simple weighted scoring and may not reflect all workshop priorities
Service cost estimates are fixed and do not account for price variations or discounts
